ca_gutenberger_wall.blurb: Gutenberger Wall is a big dome on the far bank of the Cosumnes River Gorge, outside Placerville in the Sierra foothills. It holds nineteen routes, split almost evenly between multi-pitch trad and bolted sport, from easy fifth class up to a single 5.11, with most lines between 5.8 and 5.10. The granite is water-smoothed, so expect friction and some bold, thinly protected climbing. Most routes face west to northwest and the wall is sunny from about midday into the evening. Because most visitors stay on the near side of the river and top-rope, it is quiet. Reaching the base means scrambling over wet boulders, which is hard when spring runoff is high.

ca_blind_man_s_bluff_2.blurb: Blind Man's Bluff is a small sport crag on the Mount St. Helena side of Wine Country, north of the Bay Area, at roughly 3,000 feet. Nearly all of its nineteen routes are bolted, with a single trad line. Grades start around 5.7 and run to about 5.12, with the biggest cluster in the 5.10s, so it suits a mixed group. The climbing is on pockets, huecos and knobs. Routes mostly face south-east through south-west, which means plenty of sun between mid-morning and mid-afternoon in the busy season and little shade. It is a short walk from the Bubble, and a wildfire cleared the brush that once hid it.

ca_cave_boulder.blurb: Cave Boulder is the centrepiece of the Cave Area in the Buttermilks, near Bishop on the Eastern Sierra, sitting low on the hillside in the middle of the boulder field. All nineteen problems are bouldering, and the spread is wide: a couple of easy V2s and a V3, then a strong middle band from about V5 through V10, with a V13 test piece at the top. The Buttermilker is the famous hard line, a popular short roof gives a V5, and the Cave Route is a heavily repeated V6. Expect steep, powerful climbing, so bring plenty of pads and a spotter.

ca_d_roof_area.blurb: The Roof Area is a sector of Riverside Quarry in the Inland Empire, reached from the Sierra Avenue side of town. Its nineteen routes are all bolted sport lines and all hard: roughly 5.11 to 5.13, with about half at 5.12. The wall has fairly long, vertical to slightly overhanging climbing, and a number of lines punch through the big roof overhead. This is a place for strong, experienced sport climbers rather than anyone warming up. Climbers usually come up the trail from below and walk left along the base of the cliff.

ca_fashion_slab.blurb: Fashion Slab is a quiet slab in Pine Creek Canyon above Bishop, at about 7,200 feet, a little uphill from Crack of Noon Buttress. It has around nineteen routes, ten trad and nine sport, short single pitches mostly 70 to 110 feet long. Grades run from easy up to 5.11, but most fall in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, so it is a good place for moderates. The slab faces mostly east, so it catches morning sun and gets shade later. Climbing is delicate and friction-dependent, rewarding good footwork over strength. It sees far fewer parties than the buttresses nearby.
ca_fashion_slab.parking_note: Drive a short way past the Pratt's Crack turnoff on Pine Creek Road and pull into the small gravel turnout. Stop before the creek crossing with the metal barriers, which is too far.
ca_fashion_slab.approach: A short walk of ten to twelve minutes: follow the dirt path heading southwest toward a sand dune, then scramble up and right near the dune.

ca_easy_street.blurb: Easy Street is the far end of Echo Cliffs in the Santa Monica Mountains, part of the Far Side group of walls beyond Kamikaze Cave. Its nineteen routes are all bolted sport, many of them two pitches, running from about 5.5 to 5.10, with the largest share in the 5.10s. That makes it one of the better collections of moderates in Southern California and a decent place to learn multi-pitch on bolts. Expect pockets and blocky holds on vertical to steep rock, and wear a helmet because lines are still cleaning up. The wall is shaded early and again mid-afternoon, but it can get very hot in between, and the hike in is long.
ca_easy_street.approach: A long hike of well over half an hour along the base of the cliffs, past Kamikaze Cave, to the farthest wall; the way leads through a tunnel and under a cave.
